verses.zh: 耶和华在西奈山晓谕摩西的日子，亚伦和摩西的后代如下：
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Now these are the records[NOTE:2] of Aaron and Moses when[NOTE:3] the Lord spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai.
notes: For significant literature for this chapter, see M. Aberbach and L. Smolar, “Aaron, Jeroboam, and their Golden Calves,” JBL 86 (1967): 129-40; G. Brin, “The First-born in Israel in the Biblical Period” (Ph.D. diss., University of Tel Aviv, 1971); S. H. Hooke, “Theory and Practice of Substitution,” VT 2 (1952): 2-17; and J. Morgenstern, “A Chapter in the History of the High Priesthood,” AJSL 55 (1938): 1-24.

The construction is וְאֵלֶּה תּוֹלְדֹת (ve’elleh toledot), which was traditionally translated “now these are the generations,” much as it was translated throughout the book of Genesis. The noun can refer to records, stories, genealogies, names, and accounts of people. Here it is the recorded genealogical list with assigned posts included. Like Genesis, it is a heading of a section, and not a colophon as some have suggested. It is here similar to Exodus: “these are the names of.” R. K. Harrison, Numbers (WEC), 62, insists that it is a colophon and should end chapter 2, but if that is followed in the Pentateuch, it creates difficulty throughout the narratives. See the discussion by A. P. Ross, Creation and Blessing, 69-74.
The expression in the Hebrew text (“in the day of”) is idiomatic for “when.”

verses.zh: 亚伦的儿子，长子名叫拿答，还有亚比户、以利亚撒、以他玛。
verses.en: These are the names of the sons of Aaron: Nadab the firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

verses.zh: 这是亚伦儿子的名字，都是受膏的祭司，是摩西叫他们承接圣职供祭司职分的。
verses.en: These are the names of the sons of Aaron, the anointed[NOTE:1] priests, whom he consecrated[NOTE:2] to minister as priests.[NOTE:3]
notes: The verb מָשַׁח (mashakh) means “to anoint”; here the form modifies the “priests.” The service of consecration was carried out with anointing oil (Exod 30:30). The verb is used for the anointing of kings as well as priests in the OT, and so out of that derived the technical title “Messiah” for the coming ideal king—the “Anointed One.”

In this verse the expression is in a relative clause: “who he filled their hand” means “whose hands he filled,” or “whom he consecrated.” The idiomatic expression used here is from Lev 8; it literally is “he filled their hand” (מִלֵּא יָדָם, milleʾ yadam). In the ordination service Moses placed some of the meat from the sacrifice in the hand of the ordinand, and this signified what he was going to be about—having his hand full, or being consecrated to the priesthood. There is some evidence that this practice or expression was also known in Mesopotamia. In modern ordination services a NT or a Bible may be placed in the ordinand’s hand—it is what the ministry will be about.
The form is an infinitival construction for the word for the priest, showing the purpose for the filling of the hands.

verses.zh: 拿答、亚比户在西奈的旷野向耶和华献凡火的时候就死在耶和华面前了。他们也没有儿子。以利亚撒、以他玛在他们的父亲亚伦面前供祭司的职分。
verses.en: Nadab and Abihu died[NOTE:1] before the Lord[NOTE:2] when they offered[NOTE:3] strange[NOTE:4] fire[NOTE:5] before the Lord in the desert of Sinai, and they had no children.[NOTE:6] So Eleazar and Ithamar ministered as priests[NOTE:7] in the presence of[NOTE:8] Aaron their father.
notes: The verb form is the preterite with vav (ו) consecutive, literally “and Nadab died.” Some commentators wish to make the verb a past perfect, rendering it “and Nadab had died,” but this is not necessary. In tracing through the line from Aaron it simply reports that the first two sons died. The reference is to the event recorded in Lev 10 where the sons brought “strange” or “foreign” fire to the sanctuary.
This initial clause is omitted in one Hebrew ms, Smr, and the Vulgate.

The form בְּהַקְרִבָם (behaqrivam) is the Hiphil infinitive construct functioning as a temporal clause: “when they brought near,” meaning, “when they offered.” The verb קָרַב (qarav) is familiar to students of the NT because of “corban” in Mark 7:11.
Or “prohibited.” See HALOT 279 s.v. זָר 3.

This event is narrated in Lev 10:1-7.tn The expression אֵשׁ זָרָה (ʾesh zarah, “strange fire”) seems imprecise and has been interpreted numerous ways (see the helpful summary in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC 4], 132-33). The infraction may have involved any of the following or a combination thereof: (1) using coals from some place other than the burnt offering altar (i.e., “unauthorized coals” according to J. Milgrom, Leviticus [AB], 1:598; cf. Lev 16:12 and cf. “unauthorized person” [אִישׁ זָר, ʾish zar] in Num 16:40 [17:5 HT], NASB “layman”), (2) using the wrong kind of incense (cf. the Exod 30:9 regulation against “strange incense” [קְטֹרֶת זָרָה, qetoret zarah] on the incense altar and the possible connection to Exod 30:34-38), (3) performing an incense offering at an unprescribed time (B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 59), or (4) entering the Holy of Holies at an inappropriate time (Lev 16:1-2).

The two young priests had been cut down before they had children; the ranks of the family of Aaron were thereby cut in half in one judgment from God. The significance of the act of judgment was to show that the priests had to sanctify the Lord before the people—they were to be examples that the sanctuary and its contents were distinct.
The verb is the Piel preterite from the root כָּהַן (kahan): “to function as a priest” or “to minister.”
The expression “in the presence of” can also mean “during the lifetime of” (see Gen 11:28; see also BDB 818 s.v. פָּנֶה II.7.a; cf. NASB, NIV, NCV, NRSV, TEV).

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你使利未支派近前来，站在祭司亚伦面前好服事他，
verses.en: “Bring the tribe of Levi near,[NOTE:1] and present[NOTE:2] them before Aaron the priest, that they may serve him.[NOTE:3]
notes: The use of the verb קָרַב (qarav) forms an interesting wordplay in the passage. The act of making an offering is described by this verb, as was the reference to the priests’ offering of strange fire. Now the ceremonial presentation of the priests is expressed by the same word—they are being offered to God.

The verb literally means “make it [the tribe] stand” (וְהַעֲמַדְתָּ אֹתוֹ, vehaʿamadta ʾoto). The verb is the Hiphil perfect with a vav (ו) consecutive; it will take the same imperative nuance as the form before it, but follow in sequence (“and then”). This refers to the ceremonial presentation in which the tribe would take its place before Aaron, that is, stand before him and await their assignments. The Levites will function more like a sacred guard than anything else, for they had to protect and care for the sanctuary when it was erected and when it was transported (see J. Milgrom, Studies in Levitical Terminology, 8-10).

The verb וְשֵׁרְתוּ (vesheretu) is the Piel perfect with a vav (ו) consecutive; it carries the same volitional force as the preceding verb forms, but may here be subordinated in the sequence to express the purpose or result of the preceding action.

verses.zh: 替他和会众在会幕前守所吩咐的，办理帐幕的事。
verses.en: They are responsible for his needs[NOTE:1] and the needs of the whole community before the tent of meeting, by attending to[NOTE:2] the service of the tabernacle.
notes: The Hebrew text uses the perfect tense of שָׁמַר (shamar) with a vav (ו) consecutive to continue the instruction of the preceding verse. It may be translated “and they shall keep” or “they must/are to keep,” but in this context it refers to their appointed duties. The verb is followed by its cognate accusative—“they are to keep his keeping,” or as it is often translated, “his charge.” This would mean whatever Aaron needed them to do. But the noun is also used for the people in the next phrase, and so “charge” cannot be the meaning here. The verse is explaining that the Levites will have duties to perform to meet the needs of Aaron and the congregation.

The form is the Qal infinitive construct from עָבַד (ʿavad, “to serve, to work”); it is taken here as a verbal noun and means “by (or in) serving” (see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 36, §195). This explains the verb “keep [his charge].” Here too the form is followed by a cognate accusative; they will be there to “serve the service” or “work the work.”

verses.zh: 又要看守会幕的器具，并守所吩咐以色列人的，办理帐幕的事。
verses.en: And they are responsible for all the furnishings of the tent of meeting, and for the needs of the Israelites, as they serve[NOTE:1] in the tabernacle.
notes: The Levites had the duty of taking care of all the tabernacle and its furnishings, especially in times when it was to be moved. But they were also appointed to be gatekeepers (2 Kgs 22:4; 1 Chr 9:19) in order to safeguard the purity of the place and the activities that went on there. Their offices seem to have then become hereditary in time (1 Sam 1:3); they even took on more priestly functions, such as pronouncing the benediction (Deut 10:8). See further R. de Vaux, Ancient Israel, 348-49. tn The construction uses the infinitive construct (epexegetically) followed by its cognate accusative. It would convey “to serve the service of the tabernacle,” but more simply it may be rendered as “serving.” Their spiritual and practical service is to serve.

verses.zh: 你要将利未人给亚伦和他的儿子，因为他们是从以色列人中选出来给他的。
verses.en: You are to assign[NOTE:1] the Levites to Aaron and his sons; they will be assigned exclusively[NOTE:2] to him out of all[NOTE:3] the Israelites.
notes: The verb וְנָתַתָּה (venatattah) is normally “give.” Here, though, the context refers to the assignment of the Levites to the priests for their duties. The form is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive, continuing the sequence for the imperfect of instruction.
This emphasis is derived from the simple repetition of the passive participle, נְתוּנִם נְתוּנִם (netunim netunim). See GKC 396 §123.e. The forms serve as the predicate with the subject pronoun.
The Hebrew text simply has the preposition, “from the Israelites.”

verses.zh: 你要嘱咐亚伦和他的儿子谨守自己祭司的职任。近前来的外人必被治死。」
verses.en: So you are to appoint Aaron and his sons, and they will be responsible for their priesthood,[NOTE:1] but the unauthorized person[NOTE:2] who comes near must be put to death.”
notes: The LXX includes the following words here: “and all things pertaining to the altar and within the veil.” Cf. Num 18:7.

The word is זָר (zar), usually rendered “stranger, foreigner, pagan.” But in this context it simply refers to anyone who is not a Levite or a priest, an unauthorized person or intruder in the tabernacle. That person would be put to death.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「我从以色列人中拣选了利未人，代替以色列人一切头生的；利未人要归我。
verses.en: “Look,[NOTE:1] I myself have taken the Levites from among the Israelites instead of[NOTE:2] every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. So the Levites belong to me,
notes: The particle הִנֵּה (hinneh) here carries its deictic force, calling attention to the fact that is being declared. It is underscoring the fact that the Lord himself chose Levi.
Literally “in the place of.”

verses.zh: 因为凡头生的是我的；我在埃及地击杀一切头生的那日就把以色列中一切头生的，连人带牲畜都分别为圣归我；他们定要属我。我是耶和华。」
verses.en: because all the firstborn are mine. When I destroyed[NOTE:1] all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set apart for myself all the firstborn in Israel, both man and beast. They belong to me. I am the Lord.”[NOTE:2]
notes: The form הַכֹּתִי (hakkoti) is the Hiphil infinitive construct of the verb נָכָה (nakhah, “to strike, smite, attack”). Here, after the idiomatic “in the day of,” the form functions in an adverbial clause of time—“when I destroyed.”

In the Exodus event of the Passover night the principle of substitution was presented. The firstborn child was redeemed by the blood of the lamb and so belonged to God, but then God chose the Levites to serve in the place of the firstborn. The ritual of consecrating the firstborn son to the Lord was nevertheless carried out, even with Jesus, the firstborn son of Mary (Luke 2:22-23).

verses.zh: 耶和华在西奈的旷野晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses in the desert of Sinai:

verses.zh: 「你要照利未人的宗族、家室数点他们。凡一个月以外的男子都要数点。」
verses.en: “Number the Levites by their clans[NOTE:1] and their families; every male from a month old and upward you are to number.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the house of their fathers.” So also in v. 20.
Heb “you are to/shall number them.”

verses.zh: 于是摩西照耶和华所吩咐的数点他们。
verses.en: So Moses numbered them according to the word[NOTE:1] of the Lord, just as he had been commanded.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “at the mouth of the Lord.”
The Pual perfect may be given the past perfect translation in this sentence because the act of commanding preceded the act of numbering.

verses.zh: 利未众子的名字是革顺、哥辖、米拉利。
verses.en: These were the sons[NOTE:1] of Levi by their names: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
notes: The word “sons of” does at the outset refer to the sons of Levi. But as the listing continues the expression refers more to the family groups of the various descendants.

verses.zh: 革顺的儿子，按着家室，是立尼、示每。
verses.en: These are the names of the sons of Gershon by their families: Libni and Shimei.

verses.zh: 哥辖的儿子，按着家室，是暗兰、以斯哈、希伯伦、乌薛。
verses.en: The sons of Kohath by their families were: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

verses.zh: 米拉利的儿子，按着家室，是抹利、母示。这些按着宗族是利未人的家室。
verses.en: The sons of Merari by their families were Mahli and Mushi. These are the families of the Levites by their clans.

verses.zh: 属革顺的，有立尼族、示每族。这是革顺的二族。
verses.en: From Gershon came the family of the Libnites and the family of the Shimeites; these were the families of the Gershonites.

verses.zh: 其中被数、从一个月以外所有的男子共有七千五百名。
verses.en: Those of them who were numbered, counting every male from a month old and upward, were 7,500.

verses.zh: 这革顺的二族要在帐幕后西边安营。
verses.en: The families of the Gershonites were to camp behind the tabernacle toward the west.

verses.zh: 拉伊勒的儿子以利雅萨作革顺人宗族的首领。
verses.en: Now the leader[NOTE:1] of the clan[NOTE:2] of the Gershonites was Eliasaph son of Lael.
notes: The vav (ו) disjunctive on the noun at the beginning of the verse here signals a greater emphasis on the individual rather than another item in the numbering of the clans.
Heb “a father’s house.” So also in vv. 30, 35.

verses.zh: 革顺的子孙在会幕中所要看守的，就是帐幕和罩棚，并罩棚的盖与会幕的门帘，
verses.en: And[NOTE:1] the responsibilities of the Gershonites in the tent of meeting included the tabernacle, the tent with its covering, the curtain at the entrance of the tent of meeting,
notes: The disjunctive vav (ו) here introduces a new section, listing the various duties of the clan in the sanctuary. The Gershonites had a long tradition of service here. In the days of David Asaph and his family were prominent as musicians. Others in the clan controlled the Temple treasuries. But in the wilderness they had specific oversight concerning the tent structure, which included the holy place and the holy of holies.

verses.zh: 院子的帷子和门帘（院子是围帐幕和坛的），并一切使用的绳子。
verses.en: the hangings of the courtyard,[NOTE:1] the curtain at the entrance to the courtyard that surrounded the tabernacle and the altar, and their ropes, plus all the service connected with these things.[NOTE:2]
notes: The phrases in this verse seem to be direct objects without verbs. BHS suggests deleting the sign of the accusative (for which see P. P. Saydon, “Meanings and Uses of the Particle אֵת,” VT 14 [1964]: 263-75).
Heb “for all the service of it [them].”

verses.zh: 属哥辖的，有暗兰族、以斯哈族、希伯伦族、乌薛族。这是哥辖的诸族。
verses.en: From Kohath came the family of the Amramites, the family of the Izharites, the family of the Hebronites, and the family of the Uzzielites; these were the families of the Kohathites.[NOTE:1]
notes: Both Moses and Aaron came from this line (6:16-20). During the Hebrew monarchy this branch of the line of Levi was exemplary in music (1 Chr 6:33-48). They were also helpful to Hezekiah in his reforms (1 Chr 29:12-14).

verses.zh: 按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外看守圣所的，共有八千六百名。
verses.en: Counting every male from a month old and upward, there were 8,600. They were responsible for the care[NOTE:1] of the sanctuary.
notes: The construction here is a little different. The Hebrew text uses the participle in construct plural: שֹׁמְרֵי (shomere, literally “keepers of”). The form specifies the duties of the 8,600 Kohathites. The genitive that follows this participle is the cognate מִשְׁמֶרֶת (mishmeret) that has been used before. So the expression indicates that they were responsible for the care of this part of the cult center. There is no reason to delete one of the forms (as does J. A. Paterson, Numbers, 42), for the repetition stresses the central importance of their work.

verses.zh: 哥辖儿子的诸族要在帐幕的南边安营。
verses.en: The families of the Kohathites were to camp on the south side of the tabernacle.

verses.zh: 乌薛的儿子以利撒反作哥辖宗族家室的首领。
verses.en: Now the leader of the clan of the families of the Kohathites was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.

verses.zh: 他们所要看守的是约柜、桌子、灯台、两座坛与圣所内使用的器皿，并帘子和一切使用之物。
verses.en: Their responsibilities included the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altars, and the utensils of the sanctuary with which they ministered,[NOTE:1] the curtain, and all their service.[NOTE:2]
notes: The verb is יְשָׁרְתוּ (yesharetu, “they will serve/minister”). The imperfect tense in this place, however, probably describes what the priests would do, what they used to do. The verb is in a relative clause: “which they would serve with them,” which should be changed to read “with which they would serve.”
The word is literally “its [their] service.” It describes all the implements that were there for the maintenance of these things.

verses.zh: 祭司亚伦的儿子以利亚撒作利未人众首领的领袖，要监察那些看守圣所的人。
verses.en: Now the head of all the Levitical leaders[NOTE:1] was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest. He was appointed over those who were responsible for[NOTE:2] the sanctuary.
notes: The Hebrew construction has “the leader of the leaders of” (וּנְשִׂיא נְשִׂיאֵי, unesiʾ nesiʾe).

Heb “the keepers of the responsibility” (שֹׁמְרֵי מִשְׁמֶרֶת, shomerey mishmeret). The participle is a genitive specifying the duty to which he was appointed (thing possessed); its cognate genitive emphasizes that their responsibility was over the holy place.

verses.zh: 属米拉利的，有抹利族、母示族。这是米拉利的二族。
verses.en: From Merari came the family of the Mahlites and the family of the Mushites; these were[NOTE:1] the families of Merari.
notes: The Hebrew text has “these they the families of Merari.” The independent personal pronoun has an anaphoric use, somewhat equivalent to the copula “and” (see R. J. Williams, Hebrew Syntax, 23, §115).

verses.zh: 他们被数的，按所有男子的数目，从一个月以外的，共有六千二百名。
verses.en: Those of them who were numbered, counting every male from a month old and upward, were 6,200.

verses.zh: 亚比亥的儿子苏列作米拉利二宗族的首领。他们要在帐幕的北边安营。
verses.en: Now the leader of the clan of the families of Merari was Zuriel son of Abihail. These were to camp on the north side of the tabernacle.

verses.zh: 米拉利子孙的职分是看守帐幕的板、闩、柱子、带卯的座，和帐幕一切所使用的器具，
verses.en: The appointed responsibilities of the Merarites included the frames of the tabernacle, its crossbars, its posts, its sockets, its utensils, plus all the service connected with these things,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and all their service.” This could possibly be a hendiadys: “and all their working tools.” However, the parallel with v. 26 suggests this is a separate phrase.

verses.zh: 院子四围的柱子、带卯的座、橛子，和绳子。
verses.en: and the pillars of the courtyard all around, with their sockets, their pegs, and their ropes.

verses.zh: 在帐幕前东边，向日出之地安营的是摩西、亚伦，和亚伦的儿子。他们看守圣所，替以色列人守耶和华所吩咐的。近前来的外人必被治死。
verses.en: But those who were to camp in front of the tabernacle on the east, in front of the tent of meeting, were Moses, Aaron,[NOTE:1] and his sons. They were responsible for the needs[NOTE:2] of the sanctuary and for the needs of the Israelites, but the unauthorized person who approached was to be put to death.
notes: In some Hebrew mss and Smr “and Aaron” is not in the verse. The omission arose probably by scribal error with such repetitious material that could easily give rise to variant traditions.
Here again the verb and its cognate noun are used: keeping the keep, or keeping charge over, or taking responsibility for the care of, or the like.

verses.zh: 凡被数的利未人，就是摩西、亚伦照耶和华吩咐所数的，按着家室，从一个月以外的男子，共有二万二千名。
verses.en: All who were numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered by the word[NOTE:1] of the Lord, according to their families, every male from a month old and upward, were 22,000.[NOTE:2]
notes: Here again the Hebrew has “at the mouth of,” meaning in accordance with what the Lord said. So also in v. 51.
The verb נָשָׂא (nasaʾ, “take”) has here the sense of collect, take a census, or register the names.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你要从以色列人中数点一个月以外、凡头生的男子，把他们的名字记下。
verses.en: Then the Lord said to Moses, “Number all the firstborn males of the Israelites from a month old and upward, and take[NOTE:1] the number of their names.
notes: The verb is the perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive; it carries forward the instructions from the preceding verse. The verb “take” now has the sense of appointing or designating the Levites.

verses.zh: 我是耶和华。你要拣选利未人归我，代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列所有头生的牲畜。」
verses.en: And take[NOTE:1] the Levites for me—I am the Lord—instead of all the firstborn males among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites instead of all the firstborn of the livestock of the Israelites.”
notes: The verb again is the perfect tense in sequence; the meaning of “take” may be interpreted here with the sense of “collect.”

verses.zh: 摩西就照耶和华所吩咐的把以色列人头生的都数点了。
verses.en: So Moses numbered all the firstborn males among the Israelites, as the Lord had commanded him.

verses.zh: 按人名的数目，从一个月以外、凡头生的男子，共有二万二千二百七十三名。
verses.en: And all the firstborn males, by the number of the names from a month old and upward, totaled 22,273.

verses.zh: 耶和华晓谕摩西说：
verses.en: Then the Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你拣选利未人代替以色列人所有头生的，也取利未人的牲畜代替以色列人的牲畜。利未人要归我；我是耶和华。
verses.en: “Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn males among the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites instead of their livestock. And the Levites will be mine. I am the Lord.

verses.zh: 以色列人中头生的男子比利未人多二百七十三个，必当将他们赎出来。
verses.en: And for the redemption of the 273 firstborn males of the Israelites who exceed the number of the Levites,

verses.zh: 你要按人丁，照圣所的平，每人取赎银五舍客勒（一舍客勒是二十季拉），
verses.en: collect[NOTE:1] five shekels for each one[NOTE:2] individually; you are to collect[NOTE:3] this amount[NOTE:4] in the currency of the sanctuary shekel (this shekel is 20 gerahs).[NOTE:5]
notes: The idea is expressed simply by repetition: “take five, five, shekels according to the skull.” They were to collect five shekels for each individual.
The verb form now is the imperfect of instruction or legislation.
Heb “them,” referring to the five shekels.

The sanctuary shekel was first mentioned in Exod 30:13. The half-shekel of Exod 38:26 would then be 10 gerahs. Consequently, the calculations would indicate that five shekels was about two ounces of silver for each person. See R. B. Y. Scott, “Weights and Measures of the Bible,” BA 22 (1951): 22-40, and “The Scale-Weights from Ophel, 1963-1964,” PEQ 97 (1965): 128-39.
The word used is “silver.” Coins were not in existence until after 700 b.c. (starting with Lydia).

verses.zh: 把那多余之人的赎银交给亚伦和他的儿子。」
verses.en: And give the money for the redemption of the excess number of them to Aaron and his sons.”

verses.zh: 于是摩西从那被利未人所赎以外的人取了赎银。
verses.en: So Moses took the redemption money[NOTE:1] from those who were in excess of those redeemed by the Levites.

verses.zh: 从以色列人头生的所取之银，按圣所的平，有一千三百六十五舍客勒。
verses.en: From the firstborn males of the Israelites he collected the money, 1,365 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.

verses.zh: 摩西照耶和华的话把这赎银给亚伦和他的儿子，正如耶和华所吩咐的。
verses.en: Moses gave the redemption money to Aaron and his sons, according to the word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
